title: Units and measurement
learner: Returning learners who can perform basic arithmetic but need reliable control of unit scales, dimensional meaning, reporting precision, and the interpretation of measurements.
assumedKnowledge: F01 exact fractions, powers of ten, and basic arithmetic
F03 reading labeled scales and basic linear relationships; F05 optional for log and exponential argument examples

include: Unit cancellation with powers, compound units, and temperature offsets
Explicit measurement reporting and rounding conventions
Resolution, repeatability, discrepancy, stated uncertainty bounds, and simple interval propagation
exclude: A complete physics or laboratory methods course
Instrument-specific operating or electrical safety procedures
Statistical estimation, confidence-interval derivation, and full GUM uncertainty budgets
Unspecified uncertainty combination rules or claims of metrological certification
Probability inferred from a plus/minus sign
Rounding or formatting redesign of shared graders

routes.quick: Five diagnostic probes target the five lessons. Read Quick recall and try each independent checkpoint, followed by the four-question mixed recall.
routes.full: Work the five lessons in sequence, including reasoned examples, guided questions, prediction activities, and varied practice. Use lesson notes to document your unit chain and next step.

escalation.text: The full introductory physics course and its lab are the next course destinations; their learning packs are not yet authored in this baseline. Precise free OpenStax sections provide a fuller explanation now. F01 and F03 supply authored arithmetic and graph support.

overlap: MTH 215 b02 and F01 cover exact powers and basic scientific notation.
MTH 215 b05 and F03 cover signed millisecond/meter conversions, rate units, and labeled coordinates.
MTH 215 m02-l04 and F03 cover units of a linear model and explicit tolerances.
F05 supplies dimensional exponent and logarithm-ratio examples, without replacing measurement instruction.
reuse.implementation: Wrap mth-scientific-notation as f06-scientific-notation for lesson 1 and mth-measurement-units as f06-measurement-units for lesson 2, keeping source IDs and answer rules intact. Use exact rational arithmetic for decimal scaling, rounding steps, and stated interval bounds. Precision-preserving report choices supplement numeric fields so trailing zeros can be assessed without changing the shared grader.

assessment.checkpoints: Four required independent questions per lesson, combining related fields when needed; all objective questions critical and no question beyond eight fields.
assessment.mixed: Four questions: prefixes and conversions share a multipart question with separate p1/p2 lesson targets; dimensions, reporting precision, and measurement bounds each receive a question. Mixed checks sample every lesson; lesson checkpoints provide full objective coverage.
assessment.evidence: Confidence, visits, guided tasks, and diagnostic performance do not award independent evidence. Reuse versioned attempts, independent checkpoints, notes, resume, backup, and targeted review.

sharedCapabilities.interface: Lesson.interaction adds { kind: 'refresher-measurement-lab', mode: 'prefix' | 'conversion' | 'dimensions' | 'rounding' | 'measurement', prompt: string }.
sharedCapabilities.reason: Keyboard predictions need exact unit-scale comparisons, dimensional exponent tables, precision reports, and explicit interval bounds.
sharedCapabilities.integration: One strict union member and reader dispatch. All logic and activities stay in new refresher-owned modules and reuse QuestionFields and graders. No storage, backup, app-shell, or generic answer parser changes.

verification: Independently check prefix factors using decimal exponent arithmetic and reverse conversions, including case, signed zero, tiny values, and powers 2,3,-1.
Check compound conversions using independently expanded numerator/denominator factors; verify Celsius/kelvin values and intervals separately.
Check dimensions by independent exponent bookkeeping and known derived-unit definitions; include equations with dimensionless coefficients that pass without establishing physical validity.
Use exact integer/rational rounding and a separately structured oracle; test ties, negative values, power-of-ten carries, trailing-zero reports, ambiguity, exact factors, and guard digits.

Independently enumerate interval endpoint combinations for sums, differences, products, and positive-denominator quotients; check percent bounds, zero nominal values, conversion of uncertainty, inclusive reference boundaries, and absence of invented confidence levels.
Sweep each generator structure over 100 deterministic seeds and test valid equivalent answers, invalid input, units, clear feedback, and fully rendered math.

Browser-test every checkpoint and mixed recall, specific routing, assisted/independent distinctions, notes, exact reload/resume and backup recovery, all five keyboard activities, mobile layouts, and Axe.
Run the repository unit suite, lint, typecheck, and production build before preview status; human review remains pending.
Finish and verify F06 before detailed planning for F07.
